advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove the stale 'STUB: returns an empty ran=True report' note from the `heal_fixtures` docstring now that the function is fully implemented.
evidence: heal.py:142: `    STUB: returns an empty ``ran=True`` report so the held-out oracle fails on real`
heal.py:176-219 implement the full per-criterion loop and return a populated HealReport, not an empty ran=True stub
advisory.finding: The `heal_fixtures` docstring still declares the function a STUB ('returns an empty ran=True report so the held-out oracle fails on real assertions'), but the function is fully implemented (due-stamp, gap selection, per-criterion loop, ledger reserve/finalize, quarantine filing, state persistence). The stale note misdescribes runtime behavior and will mislead maintainers.
advisory.suggested_fix: Delete the STUB paragraph from the docstring; it no longer describes the implemented behaviour.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the loop's ledger cap independent of the magic `cap_usd == 25.0` check — pass `reserve_usd=0.0` to `ledger.reserve` and use `cap_usd` directly so any cap value yields the intended effective allowance.
evidence: heal.py:258-261: `def _ledger_cap(cap_usd: float) -> float:` / `    if cap_usd == 25.0:` / `        return cap_usd + ledger.LEDGER_RESERVE_USD` / `    return cap_usd`
heal.py:178-183 calls `ledger.reserve(..., cap_usd=_ledger_cap(cap_usd))` with no `reserve_usd`
ledger.py:103 `reserve_headroom = LEDGER_RESERVE_USD if reserve_usd is None else reserve_usd` — default headroom is 30.0
ledger.py:105 `remaining = cap - reserve_headroom - spent`
advisory.finding: `_ledger_cap` adds `ledger.LEDGER_RESERVE_USD` back into the cap ONLY when `cap_usd == 25.0` exactly. Because the loop's `ledger.reserve(...)` call omits `reserve_usd`, reserve defaults to `LEDGER_RESERVE_USD` (30.0) headroom; the +reserve hack cancels it so the effective cap is 25. For ANY other `cap_usd`, the hack does not fire, reserve still subtracts the 30.0 default headroom, and the effective allowance becomes `cap_usd - 30`, silently far below (or negative relative to) the caller's intended cap.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop `_ledger_cap` and call `ledger.reserve(ledger.estimate(tier, sample_n), ledger_path=str(ledger_file), cap_usd=cap_usd, reserve_usd=0.0)` so the effective cap equals `cap_usd` for every value, not just 25.0.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] For the live (non-dry-run) heal path, refuse to run (or require an explicit repo) when no rebar repo root is resolvable instead of falling back to `Path.cwd()` and spending against it.
evidence: _llm_eval_commands.py:123-125: `repo_root = _repo_root_or_none(config)` / `if repo_root is None:` / `    repo_root = str(Path.cwd())`
_llm_eval_commands.py:132-134 then constructs `production_attempter(...)` and calls `heal_fixtures(...)` for the live (spending) path
_repo_root_or_none returns None on any exception (_llm_eval_commands.py:180-184)
advisory.finding: The live CLI heal path falls back to `Path.cwd()` when `_repo_root_or_none` returns None, then builds a production attempter and runs `heal_fixtures` which reserves/finalizes real LLM spend and writes state/ledger under `cwd/.rebar/`. Invoked outside a rebar repo this silently spends money and writes state into an arbitrary working directory rather than erroring.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a criterion leaving then re-entering the attempt list starts its failure counter fresh (seed counters={crit:2}, drop it, re-add it, assert one later failure does not immediately quarantine).
evidence: heal.py contract: 'Counters for criteria no longer in the attempt list are dropped (so a covered or quarantined — or reopened — criterion starts fresh).'
heal.py: `counters = {criterion: int(state["counters"].get(criterion, 0)) for criterion in attempted}`
search_files for 'drop' in tests/unit/test_fixture_heal_heldout.py returned (no matches); no test seeds a state counter of 2 for a criterion that then leaves/re-enters the gap.

Named violating input: state file `{"counters": {"project.alpha": 2}}`, then a run where project.alpha is quarantined/covered (leaves the attempt list) and later re-enters — its counter must restart at 0, not resume at 2 and quarantine after a single further failure.
advisory.finding: The contract-declared counter-drop/reset behavior ('Counters for criteria no longer in the attempt list are dropped … a covered or quarantined — or reopened — criterion starts fresh') is implemented by the added line `counters = {criterion: int(state["counters"].get(criterion, 0)) for criterion in attempted}` but no test exercises it. A regression that instead carried counters forward for dropped criteria would pass every existing test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a budget test at cap_usd=25.0 with a non-zero LEDGER_RESERVE_USD asserting the reserve headroom is applied (so removing `+ LEDGER_RESERVE_USD` changes the admitted set).
evidence: heal.py: `def _ledger_cap(cap_usd): if cap_usd == 25.0: return cap_usd + ledger.LEDGER_RESERVE_USD`
test_fixture_heal_heldout.py:123: `monkeypatch.setattr(ledger, "LEDGER_RESERVE_USD", 0.0)`

Named violating input: a run with cap_usd=25.0 and a non-zero LEDGER_RESERVE_USD where the reserve headroom is exactly what lets one more criterion's estimate fit — with the add-on removed it would be stopped_for_budget instead of admitted.
advisory.finding: The `_ledger_cap` branch that adds `ledger.LEDGER_RESERVE_USD` when `cap_usd == 25.0` is never observably tested at a non-zero reserve: the only budget test (AC7) sets `monkeypatch.setattr(ledger, 'LEDGER_RESERVE_USD', 0.0)`, so the add-on contributes nothing and a regression dropping the `+ ledger.LEDGER_RESERVE_USD` term would still pass.

The only CLI test (test_cli_dry_run_reports_attempt_list_with_cleared_env) runs `--dry-run`, which returns before the try/except live branch and never raises LLMError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with two open duplicate `unreliable-criterion: <id>` tickets asserting the lowest-id tie-break (criterion still skipped exactly once).
evidence: heal.py contract: 'lowest ticket id wins on a duplicate'
heal.py: `if current is None or ticket_id < current: unreliable[criterion_id] = ticket_id`
Named violating input: two open tickets both titled `unreliable-criterion: project.alpha` with distinct ids — the map must key on the lower id deterministically; no test constructs this duplicate.
advisory.finding: `_unreliable_map`'s tie-break rule ('lowest ticket id wins on a duplicate') added in this diff is untested: no test creates two OPEN `unreliable-criterion: <id>` tickets for the same criterion to assert the deterministic selection, so a regression to last-wins (or nondeterministic) selection would pass.
